name: Hildegard of Bingen
description: Renowned Rhineland mystic and scholar (d. 1179), abbess at Rupertsberg, who recorded her visions in books like Scivias and wrote on medicine, music and natural history. Rumored to have been adopted into House Jerbiton despite being unGifted.

name: Jutta
description: Anchoress who taught the young Hildegard reading and writing and was the only person she confided her visions to; died 1136.

name: Volmar
description: Monk who tutored Hildegard and helped her record her visions.

name: Richildis
description: Nun who acted as secretary to Hildegard of Bingen in recording her visions.

name: Bernard of Clairvaux
description: Saint and founding abbot of Clairvaux Abbey (1090-1153), a dominant Cistercian Church leader who preached the Second Crusade, supported the military orders and opposed heresy.

name: Pope Eugenius III
description: Pope who accepted the truth of Hildegard's visions in Scivias after Bernard of Clairvaux supported them.

name: Frederick I
description: Holy Roman Emperor with whom Hildegard of Bingen corresponded.

name: Henry II of England
description: King of England with whom Hildegard of Bingen corresponded.

name: Marie of Oignes
description: One of the founders of the beguine movement (1176-1213), a mystic who lived in poverty near the priory of Oignes, conversed with her guardian angel and had insight into the hearts of others.

name: Saint John the Evangelist
description: Saint with whom Marie of Oignes frequently conversed.

name: Elizabeth of Schönau
description: Benedictine nun and mystic (born 1129) at Schönau who recorded her visions in the Books of Visions and corresponded with Hildegard.

name: Egbert
description: Brother of Elizabeth of Schönau who helped with and influenced the reports of her visions.

name: Saint Ursula
description: Fourth-century English princess martyred with her companions at Cologne, whose bones were discovered in 1155.

name: Saint Severus of Ravenna
description: Married fourth-century archbishop of Ravenna chosen by God through a dove; a saint for married priests and their wives.

name: Vincentia
description: Wife of Saint Severus of Ravenna.

name: Innocentia
description: Daughter of Saint Severus of Ravenna and Vincentia.

name: Zita
description: Future mystic who is an infant in 1220.

name: Malfalla of Portugal
description: Future mystic who is an infant in 1220.

name: Hadewijch of Antwerp
description: Child in 1220 overcome by intense love of God, a future mystic.

name: Mechthild of Magdeburg
description: Mystic born 1210 who begins having visions of the Holy Spirit in 1222.

name: Pope Calistus II
description: Pope who decreed clerical marriages invalid at the First Lateran Council in 1123.

name: Pope Innocent II
description: Pope under whom the Second Lateran Council of 1139 confirmed the ban on clerical marriage.

name: Pope Innocent III
description: Pope whose Fourth Lateran Council of 1215 reinforced the ban on clerical marriage; Joachim of Flora died before his books could be read by him.

name: Frederick II
description: Holy Roman Emperor who ruled that offspring of clerical marriages be provided for; some Joachimites see him as the final Antichrist.

name: Saint Paul
description: Apostle who recommended that a priest without a wife can better attend to God.

name: Saint Hildegund
description: Girl disguised as a boy named Joseph who became a lay brother at the Cistercian monastery of Schönau undiscovered until her death in 1188.

name: Saint Joan
description: Legendary woman said to have held the papacy as Pope John VIII in the mid-ninth century; the story was initiated by a demon.

name: Saint Eugenia
description: Early Roman martyr who, in legend, wore men's clothing and became an abbot; patron for women seeking religious life as men.

name: Holy Maga
description: Sample Ex Miscellanea maga trained in Holy Magic by a holy hermit, dubious of Hermetic Arts, suited to aid a covenant with the Divine and Infernal.

name: Mystic Nun
description: Companion template of a noble-born nun whose mystical visions inspire verses studied by theologians.

name: Anne, a Holy Hermit
description: Companion template: Nolwenn of Finistere, who took the name Anne and lives as a hermit in a woodland cave guided by her Guardian Angel.

name: Saint Anne
description: Mother of the mother of God, much revered in Brittany; Nolwenn took her name.

name: Imposter
description: Companion template of a young noble man who, with a demon friend's help and Gender Shift, poses as a novice in a nunnery to spread corruption.

name: Anchoress
description: Grog template of a gossiping, meddlesome anchoress who knows the Church's calendar.

name: Beguine
description: Grog template of a young woman in a Flemish beguine household, with contacts among merchants' wives.

name: Priest's Wife
description: Grog template of a practical housewife married to a parish priest, a confidante of local women.

name: Saint Guthlac
description: Saint who saw his cell filled with black troops of unclean spirits, quoted from the Life of Saint Guthlac.

name: Duke of Aquitaine
description: Founder of Cluny who made the monastery free from secular authority and subject only to the pope.

name: Abbot of Cluny
description: Head of the Cluniac order holding supreme power over its houses; BaalBaruth can imitate his form.

name: Odilo
description: Fifth Abbot of Cluny who created the Feast of All Souls after a hermit's report of demons at Mount Etna.

name: Pope Benedict
description: Pope whose ghost, saved from purgatory by Cluny, appeared to bless the Festival of All Souls.

name: William of Newburgh
description: Twelfth-century chronicler who wrote of cadavers leaving their tombs to terrorize the living.

name: Peter of Bruyes
description: Defrocked twelfth-century priest who preached the Petrobrusian heresy, burning crosses and denying the value of the Sacraments.

name: Peter the Venerable
description: Great reforming Cluniac abbot who led the counter-offensive against the Petrobrusian and Henrician heresies.

name: Henry of Lausanne
description: Cluniac monk expelled for teaching Petrobrusian views; his Henrician heresy spread among Cluniac houses.

name: Owein
description: Knight who entered Saint Patrick's Purgatory and escaped by resisting temptation; his tale is well known.

name: Henry of Saltrey
description: Man who heard the knight Owein's tale and told it to Marie of France.

name: Marie of France
description: Poet who versified the tale of the knight Owein's journey through purgatory.

name: Gobert of Eze
description: Cluniac monk driven mad in purgatory who learned necromancy and began the corruption of Cluny through necromantic rites.

name: Prior of Thetford
description: Corrupt Cluniac prior in England experimenting with binding spirits into murals.

name: BaalBaruth
description: Demon duke of hell, a Spirit of Deceit and Corrupter of Monks, who supervises the corruption of the Cluniacs; appears as a great black serpent.

name: Patarus
description: Demon of the Order of Accusers serving BaalBaruth, who appears as a thin horned monk in Cluniac garb and uses powers like Whispers Behind the Back.

name: Saint Benedict of Nursia
description: Saint whose Rule the monastic orders follow; those devoted to him are protected from Patarus.

name: Saint Basil the Great
description: Saint whose devotees are immune to Patarus' powers.

name: Saint Malachy of Armagh
description: Irish Cistercian saint, friend of Bernard; obscure prophecies are falsely attributed to him.

name: Saint Almeric
description: Canonized Cistercian saint.

name: Saint Stephen the founder
description: Canonized Cistercian saint and founder.

name: Joachim of Flora
description: Charismatic Sicilian-born Cistercian abbot and prophet (d. 1200) who taught the Three Ages of the World; some Trinitarian ideas were condemned by the Fourth Lateran Council.

name: Pope Urban III
description: Pope with good relations to Joachim of Flora.

name: Pope Clement III
description: Pope with good relations to Joachim of Flora.

name: Richard the Lionheart
description: King fascinated by Joachim of Flora who consulted him about the end times before the Third Crusade.

name: Roger of Howden
description: Chronicler who reported Joachim's prophecy to Richard about Saladin.

name: Saladin
description: Muslim leader said by Joachim to be the sixth of seven persecutors of the Church; some regard him as the Antichrist.

name: Tino of Gradara
description: Aged Cistercian abbot and diabolist, illuminated while reading Joachim's books, who leads the secret Illuminati within the Cistercian order to immanentize the eschaton.

name: Jaevert
description: Demon Duke of the Deluders (Watchers), Duke of the False Millennium, who appears as an angel of light to false prophets and is behind Tino's deception.

name: Saint Francis
description: Founder of the Franciscan Friars, whose disciples the Illuminati plan to recruit.

name: Saint John Gualbert
description: Founder of the Vallumbrosans who spared his relative's murderer and saw a crucifix bow its head.

name: Peter Igneus
description: Vallumbrosan monk who led the anti-simony party in Florence and passed unscathed through a bonfire in trial by ordeal.

name: Peter Mezzobarbo
description: Bishop in Florence accused of simony who confessed after Peter Igneus survived trial by ordeal.

name: Saint Robert
description: Named as founder of the Vallumbrosan order, who ordered Peter to face trial by ordeal.

name: Varriar
description: Demon Lord of the Avengers of Evil and Lord of Discipline behind the corrupt Vallumbrosans, posing as Abbot Curtaigne; true form a huge angel of blue flame with a whip.

name: Architechtus
description: Demon perhaps summoned by the Ring of Solomon.

name: Spirit of Deceit
description: Type of demon that delights in giving false visions and disguises; BaalBaruth is of this order.

name: Order of Accusers
description: Infernal order of demons whose Whispers Behind the Back power the corrupt Cluniacs use; Patarus belongs to it.

name: Guardian Angel
description: Virtue granting an angel that guides and protects; Marie of Oignes and Anne converse with theirs.

name: Ghost
description: Spirits of the dead that appear to Cluniac monks; corrupt Cluniacs bind them into objects.

name: Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse
description: Biblical figures that may roam Mythic Europe in an apocalyptic saga.

name: Antichrist
description: Prophesied figure identified variously by Joachimites as a future pope, Frederick II or Saladin.

name: House Jerbiton
description: Hermetic House some of whose members knew Hildegard; rumored to have adopted her.

name: House Criamon
description: Hermetic House whose members try to decipher Hildegard's Unknown Language for a link between the Divine and the Enigma.

name: House Ex Miscellanea
description: Hermetic House of the Holy Maga and her parens; includes the Donatores Requietis Aeternae tradition.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The Hermetic order of magi, which may be asked to assist bishops investigating visions.

name: Donatores Requietis Aeternae
description: Ex Miscellanea tradition that arose in the Order of Hermes due to the rise of the living dead.

name: Beguines
description: Movement of lay religious women; Marie of Oignes was a founder.

name: Benedictine Order
description: Monastic order following the Rule of Saint Benedict, the norm from which the Cluniacs and others vary.

name: Order of Cluny
description: Movement within the Benedictines, effectively an independent order, famed for masses for the dead; possibly corrupted by the Infernal through necromancy and Goetia.

name: Cistercians
description: Reforming order founded at Cîteaux in 1098, the White Monks, noted for manual labor, wilderness abbeys and fighting heresy; possibly corrupted by Tino's Illuminati.

name: Vallumbrosans
description: Small, rigorously enclosed and ascetic order founded by Saint John Gualbert, with strong papal influence; possibly secretly diabolist.

name: Knights Templar
aliases: Poor Knights of the Temple of Solomon
description: Military order of warrior monks answering only to the pope, with over 7,000 members and 800 castles and preceptories.

name: Franciscans
description: Mendicant friars following Saint Francis, attracting money away from the Cluniacs.

name: Dominicans
description: Mendicant friars gaining dominance in fighting heresy.

name: Carmelites
description: Mendicant order attracting donations away from the Cluniacs.

name: Goliards
description: Clerical students who performed parodies of the Mass in protest.

name: Cathars
description: The only large-scale alternative church arising from heresy, opposed by Cistercians in the Languedoc.

name: Joachimites
description: Followers of Joachim of Flora who have adopted strange beliefs about the Antichrist and the end of the age in 1260.

name: Illuminati
description: Tino of Gradara's secret order of spiritual mystics hidden within the Cistercian order, with three degrees of initiation and an Infernalist inner circle.

name: Bavarian Illuminati
description: Adam Weishaupt's later group, a connotation to avoid.

name: Rhineland
description: Region where Hildegard lived and preached.

name: Disibodenberg
description: Benedictine abbey in the Rhineland where Hildegard and Jutta joined the nuns.

name: Rupertsberg
description: Abbey near Bingen where Hildegard was abbess from 1150.

name: Bingen
description: Town on the Rhine associated with Hildegard.

name: Eibingen
description: Place across the Rhine where Hildegard founded a nunnery in 1165.

name: Mainz
description: See whose archbishop accepted Hildegard's visions.

name: Nivelles
description: Town in Brabant where Marie of Oignes was born.

name: Brabant
description: Region of Marie of Oignes' birth and work.

name: Willambrouk
description: Place in Brabant with a leper hospital where Marie and her husband worked.

name: Oignes
description: Site of an Augustinian priory where Marie of Oignes lived and a community of lay women grew.

name: Schönau
description: Site of the Benedictine nunnery of Elizabeth and a Cistercian monastery where Hildegund lived.

name: Cologne
description: City where Saint Ursula and her companions were martyred.

name: Ravenna
description: See of Saint Severus.

name: Finistere
description: Far western coast of Brittany where Nolwenn grew up.

name: Brittany
description: Region of Anne the holy hermit.

name: Cunfin
description: Monastery in the Normandy Tribunal concealing a Hermetic covenant.

name: Cluny
description: Burgundian mother abbey of the Cluniac order.

name: Mount Etna
description: Sicilian volcano where demons were heard and an entrance to purgatory lies.

name: Saint Patrick's Purgatory
description: Place in Ireland allowing physical transition to purgatory.

name: Thetford
description: English Cluniac priory whose prior binds spirits into murals.

name: Cîteaux
description: Motherhouse of the Cistercians, founded 1098, where the annual general chapter meets.

name: Clairvaux Abbey
description: Burgundian abbey founded by Bernard of Clairvaux.

name: Mount Tabor
description: Site of the transfiguration where Joachim meditated for forty days.

name: Corazzo
description: Abbey in Calabria where Joachim took the Cistercian habit.

name: Saint Croix
description: Castle of a sympathetic noble in the Dordogne where the Illuminati inner circle meets.

name: Chorazon
description: Ruined city in the Holy Land where the Antichrist is to be born.

name: Holy Land
description: Destination of pilgrimages and crusades.

name: Vallombrosa
description: Motherhouse of the Vallumbrosans in the mountains near Florence.

name: Florence
description: City near Vallombrosa and site of a simony scandal.

name: San Silvi
description: Vallumbrosan monastery burned during the simony conflict.

name: Languedoc
description: Region where Cistercians oppose the Cathar heresy.

name: Jerusalem
description: City under whose temple Solomon's ring was reputedly found.

name: Purgatory
description: Realm of the dead's purification, physically entered by Cluniac parties.

name: Rhine Tribunal
description: Hermetic Tribunal where the Holy Maga is known as a hedge wizard; Vallumbrosans also have houses there.

name: Normandy Tribunal
description: Hermetic Tribunal where the Vallumbrosans have houses.

name: Rome Tribunal
description: Hermetic Tribunal where the Vallumbrosans have houses.

name: Iberian Tribunal
description: Hermetic Tribunal where the Vallumbrosans have houses.

name: Provencal Tribunal
description: Hermetic Tribunal where the Vallumbrosans have houses.

name: Greater Alps Tribunal
description: Hermetic Tribunal where the Vallumbrosans have houses.

name: Scivias
aliases: Know The Ways Of The Lord
description: Hildegard's tractatus on Theology recording her visions (Know The Ways Of The Lord).

name: The Book Of Life's Merits
description: Hildegard's tractatus on moral philosophy and Theology.

name: Book Of Divine Works
description: Hildegard's summa on metaphysics and Theology.

name: Physica
description: Hildegard's tractatus on natural philosophy and Medicine.

name: Causes And Cures
description: Hildegard's summa on natural philosophy and Medicine.

name: Symphony Of The Harmony Of Celestial Revelations
description: Hildegard's collection of music, a tractatus on Artes Liberales.

name: Unknown Letters and Unknown Language
description: Hildegard's writings in her own devised script, Dominion Lore tractatus, possibly Enigmatic Wisdom.

name: Play of the Virtues
description: Hildegard's morality play with music.

name: Books of Visions
description: Elizabeth of Schönau's three volumes of visions, a Theology tractatus.

name: The Book of God's Way
description: Elizabeth's summa on Church Lore warning against sins.

name: Revelations of the Sacred Company of Virgins at Cologne
aliases: Revelatio De Sacro Exercitu Virginum Coloniensium
description: Elizabeth's book on Saint Ursula's martyrs, a Dominion Lore tractatus.

name: Life of Saint Guthlac
description: Text quoted about demons attacking Saint Guthlac.

name: Institutiones Capituli Generalis
description: 1203 statutes of the Cistercian general chapter, a kind of Peripheral Code.

name: A Commentary on Isaiah and Jeremiah
description: Tino's corrupt Theology tractatus.

name: Expositio Sybillae et Merlini
description: Tino's corrupt Church Lore summa claiming to discuss prophecies of the sibyls and Merlin.

name: Ring of Saint Bernard
description: Seal ring of Solomon reputedly given to Bernard by the Templars, said to command demons.

name: True Cross
description: Relic of which could banish BaalBaruth for centuries.

name: The Gift
description: Supernatural talent for magic; Hildegard was unGifted, and the Holy Maga has it.

name: Holy Magic
description: Divine magic tradition in which the Holy Maga was initiated.

name: Dominion
description: The Divine realm's presence; Dominion auras can keep demons out.

name: Magic Aura
description: Aura of the Magic realm, which may mimic mystical experience.

name: Infernal Aura
description: Aura of the Infernal realm that increases on All Souls and grows in corrupt Cluniac houses.

name: Debauched Aura
description: Tarnished Infernal aura kept by corrupt Cluniac abbots to ease corruption.

name: Mortuary Mass
description: Funeral Mass for the living believed to kill them; an Infernal rite.

name: Black Mass
description: Perversion of the Mass possibly practiced by corrupt Cluniacs.

name: Festival of All Souls
description: Feast on November 2nd created by Odilo; on it the Dominion weakens and Infernal auras increase.

name: Chantry
description: Chapel where Cluniac monks celebrate Masses for the dead.

name: Petitioning the Church
description: Rule for seeking Church favor, with bonuses from Cluniac, Cistercian or Vallumbrosan support.

name: Heresy
description: Error in doctrine, sometimes Infernally inspired.

name: Petrobrusian heresy
description: Heresy of Peter of Bruyes denying Sacraments and burning crosses.

name: Henrician heresy
description: Heresy of Henry of Lausanne that spread among Cluniac houses.

name: Three Ages of the World
description: Joachim's teaching of the ages of Father, Son and Spirit.

name: Goetia
description: Demon-evoking sorcery used by corrupt Cluniacs.

name: Profaning the Holy
description: Blasphemous inversion of rites that creates Infernal vis.

name: Diabolic pact
description: Pact with the devil granting Virtues, signed by corrupt Vallumbrosans.

name: Maleficia
description: Spiritual gifts taught by the Illuminati's Unholy Tradition.

name: Lateran Council
description: Church councils (First 1123, Second 1139, Fourth 1215) that ruled on clerical marriage and condemned Joachim.

name: Second Crusade
description: Crusade preached by Bernard of Clairvaux.

name: Third Crusade
description: Crusade of Richard the Lionheart.

name: Rule of Saint Benedict
description: Monastic rule followed by the Benedictines, Cluniacs, Cistercians and Vallumbrosans.

name: Simony
description: Sin of buying and selling Ecclesiastical positions.

name: Ars Notoria
description: Tradition possibly referenced by the Ring of Solomon.

name: Virgil's magic
description: Ancient tradition used in a variant to animate tomb effigies.

name: Spirit Binding
